title: Ensure cross-browser compatibility, responsive layout, and reliable Internet Identity login flow

requirements.text: Fix the reported “Connection closed / service connection could not be established” issue triggered by clicking the website Login button by making the Internet Identity login flow resilient across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera/Opera GX) and by providing clear user-facing error handling when the auth popup cannot be opened or the auth session fails.

quotes:
Connection closed
It seems like the connection with the service could not be established. Try a different browser; if the issue persists, contact support. When I hit the login button of my website it brings up this make sure my website works with all browsers that includes Chrome Opera Opera GX Safari Firefox any browser you can think of it needs to be able to operate on that browser and fully function!

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking “Login” (frontend/src/components/auth/LoginButton.tsx) initiates Internet Identity login successfully on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Opera/Opera GX in a clean session.
If login fails or the auth flow cannot be established, the UI shows a clear English error message to the user (not a silent failure) and the app remains usable.
The login button cannot remain indefinitely stuck in a “Logging in...” state; the UI must recover to an actionable state (e.g., allow retry) after an appropriate failure/timeout path.
No secrets or sensitive tokens are logged to the browser console as part of any new error handling.

requirements.text: Harden actor initialization so that cross-browser differences or URL-parameter/session behaviors cannot break authenticated or anonymous app usage (including login/logout), and ensure failures in access-control initialization do not crash the app.

quotes: make sure my website works with all browsers that includes Chrome Opera Opera GX Safari Firefox any browser you can think of it needs to be able to operate on that browser and fully function!

acceptanceCriteria: The app loads and navigates normally in all target browsers even when URL parameters (e.g., the admin token parameter used by the actor initialization) are absent, blocked, or cleared.
If the actor access-control initialization fails for any reason, the failure is handled gracefully (no blank screen / unhandled promise rejection), and the user can still use non-admin public pages.
Logging out clears user session state without leaving the app in a broken state across target browsers.

requirements.text: Ensure the full website UI is fully responsive and functional across a comprehensive set of screen sizes (small Android phones, iPhones, iPads/tablets, and desktop sizes), including header navigation, mobile hamburger menu behavior, forms, dialogs/modals, and key flows (Shop, Contact, Testimonials, Admin entry guard screens).

quotes: Make sure my website is fully functional on all screen sizes phones Android phones iPhones, iPads tablets computer screens all sizes! Build it!

acceptanceCriteria: Header navigation (frontend/src/components/SiteHeader.tsx) remains usable on small screens: mobile menu opens/closes reliably, links are tappable, and content does not overflow horizontally.
All primary forms (Contact page, testimonial submission dialog, product checkout/quote path) remain readable and usable on mobile and tablet breakpoints without layout breakage.
All modals/dialogs used by the app remain accessible and scroll correctly on small screens (no content clipped off-screen with no way to reach it).
No page introduces horizontal scrolling at common viewport widths (e.g., 360px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px) except where explicitly intended for content.

requirements.text: Add a lightweight cross-browser QA checklist and automated smoke coverage (where feasible within the existing React app tooling) focused on the login button/auth flow and critical navigation, to prevent regressions of the reported connection/login issue.

quotes: make sure my website works with all browsers ... and fully function!

acceptanceCriteria: A documented QA checklist exists in-repo (English) specifying the minimum manual verification steps for Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Opera/Opera GX, including the Login flow and basic navigation.

At least one repeatable smoke test (or equivalent automated check supported by the current project setup) covers that the app renders, navigation works, and the login button does not hard-crash the UI when invoked.

constraints: Do not edit files under frontend/immutablePaths (including frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts and frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts if they are marked immutable in the system context; if not immutable, still avoid changing authentication semantics beyond stability/error handling).
Keep all user-facing text in English.
Do not add any third-party authentication beyond Internet Identity.
Do not expose or log any admin verification codes, master override codes, or other secrets while implementing error handling and QA.
nonGoals: Guaranteeing compatibility with every browser ever made; the explicit target set is Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera/Opera GX, plus maintaining generally standards-based behavior elsewhere.
Adding new app features unrelated to cross-browser stability, login reliability, or responsive layout.
